:::{#hero}

I am a biostatistician based in Mainz, Germany. For six years I worked at the
Institute of Medical Biostatistics, Epidemiology and Informatics (IMBEI),
Universitätsmedizin Mainz, on oncology biostatistics and investigator-initiated
clinical trials, alongside health-services research.

My methodological focus is **applied Bayesian modelling and design** — Bayesian
compartment modelling of MRI time-series, Bayesian additive regression trees on
high-dimensional omics, precision-based sample-size determination, and a Bayesian
zero-inflated negative binomial primary trial analysis.

I am completing a PhD in the Faculty of Biology at Johannes Gutenberg University
Mainz on omics-based biomarker discovery for familial pancreatic cancer using
machine learning.

:::

## What I do

**Clinical trial statistics.** Statistical analysis plans on the ICH E9(R1) estimand
framework, sample-size and power calculations, primary-endpoint analysis, and the
statistical sections of ethics-committee and funder submissions.

**Machine learning on omics data.** Model-based gradient boosting with stability
selection, Bayesian additive regression trees and Gaussian graphical models applied
to high-dimensional proteomics and LC-MS metabolomics, with explainable-ML methods
to make model behaviour interpretable to clinical collaborators.

**Statistical consulting.** Six years advising doctoral candidates and research
groups across more than fifteen clinical departments — translating clinical
questions into designs, endpoints and analysis plans, and delivering
publication-ready results.
